summary.text: Clyde Jones is a retired U.S. Army First Sergeant (1984-2005), Baptist associate minister and corporate safety coordinator, and the Democratic nominee for Alabama's 1st Congressional District. He is a first-time candidate for federal office and advanced to the general election without a primary opponent. He is running on affordability, restoring checks and balances in Congress, healthcare for all and immigration reform.

paragraphs.text: Native of Charles City, Virginia; earned a high school diploma from Charles City High School.
Served 21 years in the U.S. Army Signal Corps (1984-2005), retiring as a First Sergeant; received the Bronze Star Medal for service in Operation Desert Storm and Operation Iraqi Freedom II.
Earned a bachelor's degree in liberal arts, with a focus on administration and management, from Excelsior University in 2008.

Relocated to South Alabama in January 2013 for a job with DuPont and moved with his family to Baldwin County that August; retired from FMC Agriculture Solutions as a Process Safety Management Coordinator in May 2024.
Serves as an Associate Minister at Macedonia Missionary Baptist Church in Daphne, Alabama.

Served two years as President of the Board of Directors for the nonprofit Alabama Arise and sits on the Steering Committee for Leadership Baldwin and the Executive Committee for the Commission on Social Justice and Racial Reconciliation of the Episcopal Diocese of the Gulf Coast.

According to his campaign website, has chaired the Education, Political, and Veterans Affairs Committee of the Baldwin County NAACP and served as president of the board of Supporting Educational Excellence in Daphne Schools (SEEDS); he is married to Nichelle Barnes Jones and they have three children and six grandchildren.
Advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after the primary was canceled; this is his first campaign listed on Ballotpedia.
